newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly firmer, gas oil lower.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly firmer, gas oil lower.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly firmer on Tuesday, except gas oil.
Gasoline prices rose slightly as refiners began to see less product available and no arbitrage to northern Europe.
Dealers said high octane was particularly scarce.
Prices rose towards parity with those in the north after some U.S.-bound tankers loaded low octane gasoline on a back-haul having delivered low sulphur gas oil to Europe.
Naphtha was steady after a trader covered his short into the north at $232.25 cif for an Alexandria cargo.
Two Algerian cargoes which were delayed for two weeks finally loaded, but the port was closed again on Tuesday due to high winds, a broker said.
Gas oil eased with the IPE, but premiums to the IPE firmed slightly for heating oil, traders said.

They reported good demand into Lebanon and West Africa, with a Romanian cargo trade around quotes fob high +$8 cif Lebanon for a 0.2 percent sulphur cargo. While most trade was on floating prices, one dealer saw a heating oil bid at Nov IPE +$6 cif Med, $1-2 above Monday's premium.
High sulphur cracked cargoes were talked a touch under $120 fob Med with interest essentially restricted to bunker demand in Gibraltar which could be met by NWE material.
The low sulphur sector was very quiet with swaps pointing to higher numbers in NWE, but Med physical prices reluctant to leave $135 cif Italy.
"We had $132 on Friday which was very low and nothing since," said one dealer. Another commented "we need some cold weather to kick start prices".
